texts.li: [game,winter] {PET_nameDef} came back across the snow dragging {BEAST}, and wouldn't let go of it until {A_nameDef} had made a proper fuss. There's fresh meat for the pot, in the middle of winter.

[game] {A_nameDef} heard a commotion in the brush, and {PET_nameDef} came out of it backward, tugging {BEAST} by the leg. {PET_nameDef} has been lying by it all morning, waiting for someone to notice.

[herbs,lowtech] {PET_nameDef} has been rolling in something by the stream, and came home smelling of it, with a mouthful of the plant itself. It turned out to be a healing herb, and {A_nameDef} went back with a basket for the rest.
[herbs] {A_nameDef} followed {PET_nameDef} to see where {PET_pronoun} keeps going, and found a patch of healing herbs in a hollow nobody had noticed. {PET_nameDef} had already eaten some.
[purse,lowtech] {PET_nameDef} brought {A_nameDef} a little cloth bag tied with string, soaked and chewed. There were {COUNT} silver coins inside, and nobody here has lost any.
[purse] {PET_nameDef} has been digging by the old road, and this morning came back with a purse in {PET_possessive} teeth and {COUNT} silver in the purse. {A_nameDef} has decided not to ask where.
[component] {PET_nameDef} trotted in from the junk pile with a component in {PET_possessive} mouth, set it down carefully at {A_nameDef}'s feet, and waited. It works.
[nothing] {PET_nameDef} brought {A_nameDef} a very large stick, the largest {PET_pronoun} could carry, and laid it across the doorway. {A_nameDef} has thanked {PET_objective} for it twice.
[nothing,winter] {PET_nameDef} came in from the snow with a frozen turnip, dropped it in {A_nameDef}'s lap and lay down on {A_possessive} feet. {A_nameDef} has kept the turnip.

[fossil] {A_nameDef} found a stone by the stream with a pattern of ridges on it, and after a lot of scrubbing it turned out to be a fern, older than anything. {A_nameDef} has been carrying it around in both hands.\n\n{B_nameDef} could tell {A_objective} what it is, if there's time.

[coin,lowtech] {A_nameDef} turned up a coin in the vegetable patch, thin and bent, with a king on it that nobody here has heard of. {A_nameDef} wants to know which king, and where his kingdom went.\n\n{B_nameDef} might know.

[coin,!lowtech] {A_nameDef} dug up an old coin by the gate, stamped with a ship and a date from before anyone's grandparents. {A_nameDef} has been asking everyone what the ship was.\n\n{B_nameDef} might be able to tell {A_objective}.

[skull] {A_nameDef} found a small animal's skull under the hedge, clean and white, with teeth that still meet. {A_nameDef} has named it and wants to know what it was.\n\n{B_nameDef} has offered to look at it with {A_objective}.

[geode,winter] {A_nameDef} found a round stone under the snow by the stream and cracked it on the step. Inside it was hollow and full of crystal, like frost that doesn't melt.\n\n{B_nameDef} could explain how it got there.

[machine] {A_nameDef} found a small machine in the scrap pile with a wheel that still turns, and has been turning it all day. {A_nameDef} wants to know what it did.\n\n{B_nameDef} could take it apart with {A_objective} and find out.

[winter] Snowed in with the colony for a night, {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has had plenty of time to look at {A_nameDef}, and to remember where {X_pronoun} saw that face: on a notice, from when {A_nameDef} was {TALE}, with a price under it.\n\n{X_nameDef} would forget it for {COUNT} silver.

[colony:Merciful] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has heard the colony forgives a lot, and wants to see if it will pay too. {X_nameDef} knows what {A_nameDef} was, {TALE}, and remembers the reward. Silence costs {COUNT} silver.

[winter] A rider of {FACTION} came through the snow with a letter for {A_nameDef}, from {X_nameDef}, {A_possessive} old commander, who is fighting {ENEMY} through the winter and running short. {X_nameDef} asks for {TALE}, for old times' sake.\n\nA share of the spoils will come back, if they win.

[healer,lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} came to the gate leaning on a stick, and asked for {A_nameDef}. Years ago {A_nameDef} cut an arrowhead out of {X_possessive} side by firelight. {X_nameDef} has come to say thank you, and has brought a gift.

[doctor,winter] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} walked through the snow to find {A_nameDef}, who once stitched {X_objective} up on a bad night on the road. {X_nameDef} has a gift, and wanted to give it in person.

[past:farmer] {A_nameDef} found a map stitched into the back of an old seed sack: the family's old farm, with a corner of a field marked where something was buried in a bad year. It's a few days' travel from the colony.

[past:artisan] Unpicking an old tool roll, {A_nameDef} found a scrap of map tucked in the lining, with a workshop marked a few days' travel from here. {A_nameDef} remembers the master who owned it hiding things under the floor.

[farming,other] {A_nameDef}'s plow caught on something under the field: an old crate, sealed tight, with a lock that hasn't turned in years.\n\n{B_nameDef} thinks it can be opened properly with some patience. It could also be broken open, or sold sealed to {FACTION} for {COUNT} silver.

[winter,other] {A_nameDef} found the corner of a crate sticking out of the frozen ground and spent half a day chipping it free. It's sealed and heavy.\n\n{B_nameDef} wants to try the lock. It could also be broken open, or sold sealed to {FACTION} for {COUNT} silver.

[skill:Mining] {A_nameDef} heard the slide from bed, a long grinding roar in the hills {PLACE}, and was out at first light to look. The rubble has closed off the ground there until someone mines through it.\n\n{A_nameDef} came back delighted: the torn hillside shows a seam of {THING}.

[skill:Artistic] The storm split the old {BEAST} near the colony, and {A_nameDef} was out in the rain looking at it before the thunder had stopped. The heartwood is dark and hard, and {A_nameDef} already knows what {A_pronoun} would carve.\n\nFelled, it would give about {COUNT} wood, or it could be left standing.

[industrial] Lightning hit the old {BEAST} by the colony last night and left it split and smoking. The heartwood has dried hard and dark. {A_nameDef} wants to carve from it.\n\nIt would also cut into about {COUNT} wood, or it could be left standing.

[summer,fields] A wild swarm has taken over a hollow tree by the fields, and the crops are humming with them from dawn to dusk. {A_nameDef} thinks {A_pronoun} could smoke them out and take the comb. Left alone, they'll keep working the fields.

[nofields,summer] Wild bees have filled a hollow tree near the colony with comb, and the honey is running out of a crack in the bark. {A_nameDef} thinks {A_pronoun} could smoke them out and take it.\n\nOr they could be left alone.

[winter] A falling star came down {PLACE} last night and melted itself a hole in the snow. {A_nameDef} found it at dawn, black and pitted and still steaming.\n\nIt's good iron. {A_nameDef} wants to forge a {TALE} from it.
[wood,summer] A summer storm up in the hills sent the river over its banks for a day. It's back where it belongs now, and has left {COUNT} wood strewn along the banks.
[snag,lowtech] The flood went down and left the banks heaped with driftwood, {COUNT} wood in all. Wedged in the roots of one log was something else, and {A_nameDef} fished it out: {TALE}.

[!lowtech] An old {BEAST} walked out of the morning fog and stopped by the fence, looking at the colony. It hasn't moved since. Even people who don't believe in signs have been out to look at it.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants to follow it when it goes. It could also be left an offering, or hunted.
